title: Tax Laws Amendment (2013 Measures No. 4) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would restrict access to research tax incentives, allow eligible businesses to receive quarterly research refunds and change rules for refunding overpaid goods and services tax.
Companies with aggregated assessable income of $20 billion or more would lose the research incentive for income years starting from 1 July 2013.
Quarterly credits would cover quarters from 1 January 2014; refunds of overpaid goods and services tax passed to customers would generally require reimbursement.
changes: Quarterly credits would be reconciled against actual refund entitlements when annual income tax assessments were made.
Businesses could use standard quarterly amounts or vary them, with interest applying to excessive variations.
Companies excluded by the income threshold could claim ordinary tax treatment for research spending, including available deductions.
The Commissioner would retain discretion to refund excess tax in exceptional circumstances.
summary.affected: Research companies, businesses seeking refunds of overpaid goods and services tax, their customers and the Commissioner of Taxation are affected.
